newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - December 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Friday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Police compose facial sketch for killer of women's rights activist Peng Wen-ju.
Taiwan to stop referring to Hong Kong and Macau as "regions" after they return to China's rule in 1997.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - District court judge detained on charges he blackmailed girlfriend for money.
Countries attending World Trade Organisation meeting in Singapore agree to lower tariffs on information technology products.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Forward foreign exchange trading to be liberalised completely next week.
Government decides not to grant public projects automatically to lowest bidders.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang says Lee Teng-hui welcome to visit mainland under principle of "one China".
Foreign securities house predicts Taiwan stock index may reach 8,000 points by end 1997.
LIBERTY TIMES - Police investigate whether detainee Chang Chung-teh is killer of Taoyuan county magistrate, seven others.
Missing Tainan government investigator found dead.
